items.stem: A chat tool built on the Messages API forgets a customer's name after the server process restarts, though she introduced herself earlier. What is the likeliest cause?

options.a: The weights inside the model were reset by the restart itself
options.b: The window shrinks each time a server process is restarted
options.c: The history was not sent again along with the new call
options.d: The name was longer than the output limit of the call

items.explanation: The Messages API is stateless: code must resend the history on every request.

items.stem: A team budgets an English document at one token per word and is surprised by the bill. What is the better rule of thumb?

options.a: About three and a half characters each, then count with the endpoint
options.b: One piece for every sentence on average, in any language
options.c: Exactly four characters for each piece in every language
options.d: The same figure as any earlier model gives for identical text

items.explanation: A Claude token is about 3.5 English characters, it varies with language and tokenizer, and counts are estimates to recheck per model.

items.stem: Input of 180,000 tokens goes to a model with a 200K window, with max_tokens set to 40,000. What does the course say happens on Claude 4.5 models and newer?

options.a: The API returns a 400 error telling you that the prompt is too long
options.b: The API quietly trims the input until the total fits
options.c: The output cap is raised automatically to match the space
options.d: The call is accepted, and generation may stop early at the limit

items.explanation: Only input alone larger than the window is refused; input plus max_tokens beyond it is accepted and generation can stop at the limit.

items.stem: A team wants repeatable labels from Claude Sonnet 5.5. Which approach follows the course?

options.a: Set the temperature to 0.2 on every request that is sent
options.b: Constrain the output to a fixed list and validate in code
options.c: Add a line saying be consistent at the top of the prompt
options.d: Run each ticket five times and keep the most common label

items.explanation: The current models reject non-default sampling values, a prompt sentence does not remove sampling, and extra runs only detect variation.

items.stem: A model asked about last month's release notes answers confidently from an older version. Which fix sits at the right layer?

options.a: Ask it to try harder to remember the newest version
options.b: Raise max_tokens so that it has longer to think the answer through
options.c: Switch to a model with a larger window and ask again
options.d: Supply the text in the context, or give it a tool to fetch it

items.explanation: Knowledge stops at the cutoff and the model has no live access; recent or private facts must come through the context or a tool.

items.stem: Which statement about a model's knowledge is correct?

options.a: It updates itself each time any user corrects one of its answers
options.b: It stops at the cutoff, so recent or private facts must be supplied
options.c: It includes anything stored in the files on the user's own computer
options.d: It always knows today's date from the clock of the server

items.explanation: The weights are fixed after training and the model has no clock, no access to your files and no knowledge after the cutoff.

items.stem: An engineer asks why Claude cannot reliably count the letters in a long identifier. Which explanation is best?

options.a: Its vocabulary is too small to hold any identifier
options.b: Its context window is shorter than the identifier is
options.c: It reads pieces of text rather than single characters
options.d: Its training stopped before identifiers like that existed

items.explanation: The tokenizer cuts text into sub-word pieces, so exact character work is approximate and belongs in code.

items.stem: A stakeholder expects the assistant to improve each week as colleagues correct it in chat. Why will that not happen by itself?

options.a: Using the model never changes the trained weights themselves
options.b: Corrections are deleted automatically after thirty days
options.c: Correction messages are too short for the model to register
options.d: The app switches to a different model every single week

items.explanation: Training changes weights and inference does not; memory features only put saved notes back into the context.

items.stem: Which stages turn a text-continuing pretrained model into a helpful assistant?

options.a: Fine-tuning plus preference learning applied afterwards
options.b: A larger tokenizer vocabulary added once training is done
options.c: A longer context window added once training is done
options.d: A lower temperature applied at inference time by default

items.explanation: Fine-tuning, RLHF and Constitutional AI shape behaviour; window size and sampling do not.

items.stem: Constitutional AI replaces much of the human preference labelling with what?

options.a: More paid raters who compare every pair of replies by hand, one at a time
options.b: A written list of principles used to critique and compare answers
options.c: A fixed list of banned words applied after generation ends
options.d: A search engine that fetches approved answers to reuse

items.explanation: The model critiques and revises its answers against principles, then reinforcement learning uses AI feedback.

items.stem: A manager says the model is trained to be honest, so its numbers need no check. What is the best reply?

options.a: That is true, because honesty training guarantees every single figure it gives
options.b: That is true for numbers but not for names or other facts
options.c: That is false only for the models older than the Opus tier
options.d: That is a goal, not a guarantee, so claims that matter get verified

items.explanation: HHH is a research framework that informs training, not a guarantee about any single answer.

items.stem: A company wants Claude to answer from a product manual that changes monthly. Which route does the module support?

options.a: Fine-tune the model again on each new edition that appears
options.b: Wait for the next model release to pick up the changes
options.c: Put the current edition into the context at request time
options.d: Teach the model the changes through many repeated chats

items.explanation: The Claude API does not currently offer fine-tuning, and knowledge you have belongs in the window.

items.stem: A team must choose a tier for varied hard reasoning and is unsure. What approach does the documentation back?

options.a: Pick the highest-priced tier as the safe default choice for every task
options.b: Run its own prompts and data across candidates, then compare
options.c: Choose the model whose name is the shortest to type
options.d: Use the cheapest tier and accept whatever it produces

items.explanation: The decision rule is to benchmark on your own use case; a good evaluation set is the most important step.

items.stem: Which surface suits a developer who wants an agent to edit files and run commands in a repository?

options.a: A Project in the app with the files pasted into it
options.b: Claude in Chrome on the repository's web page
options.c: The Claude for Excel add-in, opened on a spreadsheet of the files
options.d: Claude's own coding tool for working inside a codebase

items.explanation: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that reads a codebase, edits files and runs commands.

items.stem: Which statement about Claude Haiku 4.5 is right?

options.a: It has a 200K window and the nearest retirement date listed
options.b: It has a 1M window and adaptive thinking that is always enabled
options.c: It is the top tier that sits above the Opus model
options.d: It is priced above Sonnet 5.5 for both input and output

items.explanation: Haiku 4.5 is the fastest and lowest-priced tier with a 200K window, and retires not sooner than 2026-10-15.

items.stem: Which setting trades intelligence for latency and cost within a single model?

options.a: The size of the context window for the request
options.b: The prefill text at the start of the reply
options.c: The effort level for the request
options.d: The batch discount applied to the request

items.explanation: The documentation describes effort that way and says tuning it is often a better lever than switching models.

items.stem: Which design puts most tokens on the cheaper model while keeping a stronger one for hard calls?

options.a: Running every single request on the top tier for safety
options.b: Doubling the effort setting on every request it handles
options.c: An orchestrator that hands bulk work to lower-cost workers
options.d: Sending each request to two tiers and averaging the replies

items.explanation: Executor-advisor and orchestrator-worker patterns are the documented answer to mostly easy and occasionally hard work.

items.stem: A prompt behaves differently when sent to the API and when typed into a Project in the app. What is the likeliest reason?

options.a: Each surface wraps its own instructions, tools and defaults around it
options.b: The two surfaces rely on entirely unrelated model families
options.c: The app rewrites every message into another language first
options.d: The API removes the final sentence of every prompt it gets

items.explanation: The same model sits behind many surfaces, but what is sent around your text differs.

items.stem: A photographed table is rotated and very small, and Claude misreads one number. Which documented limit applies?

options.a: Claude cannot read tables in any picture that anyone gives it at all
options.b: Claude refuses every image that has numbers in it
options.c: Images are limited to a single one per request
options.d: Poor-quality or awkwardly turned pictures can lead to mistakes

items.explanation: The vision page lists low-quality, rotated and very small images, and asks you to verify readings.

items.stem: A product owner wants a model to decide a customer's loan eligibility alone. What does the course advise?

options.a: Let the model decide, then tell the customer afterwards
options.b: Keep a qualified person in charge, with the tool as an aid
options.c: Use the largest tier so that no review is needed
options.d: Use deep thinking so that a separate check is unnecessary

items.explanation: Decisions with legal, medical, financial or safety consequences stay with a qualified person.

items.stem: When is turning thinking up most worthwhile?

options.a: Short lookups and one-word labels where speed matters most to the user
options.b: Rewriting a sentence in a friendlier tone for a reader
options.c: Fetching today's date from the model's own memory
options.d: Multi-step maths, hard debugging or analysis with many facts

items.explanation: Thinking helps on complex tasks and is billed as output, so it is wasted on simple ones.

items.stem: An agent will operate a web page through screenshots. Which precaution matters most?

options.a: Give it the user's saved passwords so nothing blocks it
options.b: Run it in isolation with no secrets, and confirm consequential steps
options.c: Turn screenshots off entirely so that costs stay down
options.d: Trust any instruction that appears on whichever page it happens to visit

items.explanation: A screen is untrusted input that can carry injected instructions.

items.stem: A report needs the total of 4,000 line amounts. Which design is best?

options.a: Claude adds the figures in a single pass through them
options.b: Claude adds them twice and the team averages the two
options.c: A script does the addition and Claude explains the result
options.d: Claude estimates the sum from a sample of the lines

items.explanation: Exact arithmetic belongs in code; the model approximates.

items.stem: Which job needs no extra machinery around Claude?

options.a: Summarising an uploaded article for a colleague
options.b: Totalling a column of invoice figures to the cent
options.c: Reporting yesterday's exchange rate between two currencies
options.d: Looking up a value in the company's own database

items.explanation: Language-shaped drafting and summarising suit a model, while exact, recent or private facts need code, tools or retrieval.

items.stem: Which step of a monthly sales commentary should stay with a person?

options.a: Deciding which of the variances matter to the board
options.b: Drafting the narrative text that explains the variances
options.c: Formatting the finished text into the board template
options.d: Summarising last quarter's meeting notes for the file

items.explanation: Judgment that carries accountability stays with a person, while drafting and formatting suit Claude.

items.stem: Which part of a description tells Claude how to behave, such as flagging anything it is unsure about?

options.a: The product element
options.b: The performance element
options.c: The process element
options.d: The provenance element

items.explanation: The three parts are product (what you want), process (how to go about it) and performance (how Claude should behave).

items.stem: Which question checks an output for completeness?

options.a: Does the tone of the reply sound confident enough?
options.b: Is the name of the saved file tidy and consistent?
options.c: Is the answer long enough to look properly thorough to a reader?
options.d: What would a careful reader expect to see that is missing?

items.explanation: Completeness is about silent omissions, which a summary can have even when every sentence is accurate.

items.stem: A colleague asks how reliable Claude's confident tone is as a signal. What is the course's answer?

options.a: It usually means that a fact has already been verified
options.b: Only hedged wording ever needs a second look from a careful reader
options.c: It proves nothing, so check what matters against the source
options.d: It matters only when the text is a legal document

items.explanation: Confidence of tone is not a signal; check the claims that would hurt if wrong against the source of record.

items.stem: Who answers for a mistake in AI-assisted work that you forwarded to others?

options.a: The vendor that built the model that drafted it
options.b: You do, whoever drafted the text in the first place
options.c: The colleague who first suggested using the tool
options.d: Nobody, since an automated draft carries no author

items.explanation: You own what you send; accountability for errors stays with the person.

items.stem: Which routine fits a team that lets an agent do several steps itself?

options.a: Unlimited access, because speed matters more than any kind of control
options.b: Review only after a complaint has arrived from someone
options.c: No record of the steps, in order to save storage
options.d: A defined scope, review before consequences, and a record kept

items.explanation: Treat an agent like a new colleague with limited access.

items.stem: A prompt asks for a reply that is concise, thorough, clear and professional, and results vary. Which fix is best?

options.a: Swap the adjectives for limits you can measure, like a word cap
options.b: Add a few more adjectives so that the intent is clearer
options.c: Switch to a larger tier and keep the same wording
options.d: Add a role line that uses a famous and senior job title

items.explanation: Stacked adjectives conflict and cannot be checked; give constraints you could verify afterwards.

items.stem: Where should a pasted document go in a long prompt?

options.a: Between two copies of the question, one on each side
options.b: At the very end, after all of the instructions
options.c: Near the top, with the question placed after it
options.d: Anywhere at all, since order never makes a difference

items.explanation: The documentation places long inputs above the query and reports better results with queries at the end.

items.stem: How many examples does the best-practices page suggest for best results?

options.a: A single one, in order to avoid overfitting
options.b: Twenty or more, in every case without exception
options.c: Three to five relevant ones that vary enough
options.d: None at all, since examples harm the output

items.explanation: The page says to include 3 to 5 examples that mirror the use case and cover edge cases.

items.stem: Which route replaces prefilling the reply on current models?

options.a: Structured outputs or an enum tool, plus direct instructions
options.b: A longer system prompt that repeats the format twice
options.c: A higher temperature setting chosen for each request
options.d: A second prefill placed in the user turn instead

items.explanation: From the 4.6 models on, prefilled responses are no longer supported.

items.stem: What should a template builder do with untrusted text placed between tags?

options.a: Trim it down to its first line, whatever the rest of it contains
options.b: Convert all of it to lower case before inserting it
options.c: Place it above the instructions instead of below
options.d: Escape the angle brackets so it cannot close its own tag

items.explanation: Position is not a boundary; tags, a data statement and escaping do the marking.

items.stem: In what order does the course say to improve a weak output?

options.a: Rewrite everything at once, then test a single case to see what happens
options.b: Diagnose the cause, change one thing, re-run the same inputs
options.c: Change the model first, then rework the prompt text
options.d: Add examples until it seems to work, then stop

items.explanation: The controlled fix is diagnosis, one change and a re-run of the whole evaluation set.

items.stem: Which item belongs in a Project's instructions rather than its knowledge?

options.a: The current price list for all of the products
options.b: A scanned contract from one of the suppliers
options.c: Last quarter's report on the sales figures
options.d: The tone and format every reply should follow

items.explanation: Instructions say how to work; knowledge says what is true here.

items.stem: A team lead wants colleagues to read but not change a Project. Which permission level fits?

options.a: Can edit access
options.b: Can view access
options.c: Creator access
options.d: Public access

items.explanation: Can view is read-only access to contents, knowledge and instructions.

items.stem: What does RAG mode do for a large Project?

options.a: Deletes the older chats once the limit is reached
options.b: Shares the Project with the whole organisation at once
options.c: Retrieves the relevant parts so that more material fits
options.d: Switches the model to a smaller and cheaper tier

items.explanation: On paid plans it expands capacity by up to 10 times by retrieving relevant parts.

items.stem: Which statement about an artifact's storage is right?

options.a: It may be shared, so check before entering sensitive data
options.b: It is always private to the person who created it
options.c: It can hold images and files as well as text
options.d: It has no size limit of any kind attached to it

items.explanation: Storage is text only, up to 20 MB, personal or shared; shared storage is visible to every user.

items.stem: Which pair of requirements must hold before Research can run?

options.a: A paid plan, and live web lookup enabled
options.b: A shared Project, and a connector that is enabled
options.c: An artifact, and a skill that is enabled
options.d: The desktop app, and a folder connected to it

items.explanation: Research is for paid plans and needs web search switched on.

items.stem: Which statement about skills is correct?

options.a: All of them are loaded into every single chat
options.b: Only the relevant ones are loaded into context when needed
options.c: They can run only inside Claude Code and nowhere else
options.d: They need no review at all before being shared

items.explanation: Progressive disclosure keeps unused skills out of the context window.

items.stem: What can an owner set for each tool of a connector?

options.a: Fast, balanced or slow, depending on the plan
options.b: Public, internal or secret, depending on the file
options.c: Read-only, read-write or admin, depending on the role
options.d: Always allowed, needs approval, or blocked

items.explanation: Per-tool action restrictions work alongside the source system's permissions.

items.stem: Which workload suits Cowork over chat?

options.a: A one-line definition of a term for a colleague who asked
options.b: A quick brainstorm of names for a new product line
options.c: A deliverable built from a folder of files and several tools
options.d: A translation of a single sentence into French and German

items.explanation: Cowork suits a clear deliverable that touches files or tools; chat suits light, turn-by-turn work.

items.stem: In Claude in Chrome, which mode means nothing checks the actions?

options.a: Manually approve
options.b: Skip all approvals
options.c: Automatically approve
options.d: Site allowlist mode

items.explanation: Skip all approvals means Claude does not pause and nothing checks its actions.

items.stem: Which statement about the Microsoft 365 add-ins' data is right?

options.a: They inherit every custom retention setting that is set
options.b: Their chats are kept on Anthropic's servers indefinitely
options.c: They keep no data of any kind for any length of time
options.d: Their activity is missing from the Enterprise audit logs

items.explanation: The add-ins do not inherit custom retention and are outside the audit logs, though the Compliance API can include them.

items.stem: Who sees Claude Tag's work when it is tagged in a channel?

options.a: Every member there, using the access set for that space
options.b: Only the person who tagged it, as a private reply
options.c: Only the Slack admins who installed the application
options.d: Only the history of the requester's private account

items.explanation: Channel work is visible to all members and uses the access an admin set for it; a DM is personal.

items.stem: Which action stays off limits for Claude in Chrome in every mode?

options.a: Reading the text of a page that is open
options.b: Filling in a harmless form on a trusted site
options.c: Completing a purchase on a shopping site
options.d: Taking a screenshot of the tab that is active

items.explanation: Purchases, account creation and permanent deletions are prohibited whatever the permission mode.

items.stem: What does Cowork's isolated cloud environment protect?

options.a: Everything that Claude is able to read for you
options.b: The mailbox that has been connected to the task
options.c: Your home and company network, but not what tools expose
options.d: The files that sit inside any connected folder

items.explanation: The isolation does not limit what Claude reads or does through connected tools.

items.stem: Which Claude Tag setup step needs the Owner role?

options.a: Pairing the Slack workspace with the organisation
options.b: Mentioning Claude in a channel it has already joined
options.c: Sending Claude a direct message about a task
options.d: Reading a thread that Claude has already answered

items.explanation: Setup needs the Owner role in a Team or Enterprise organisation and a Slack workspace admin.

items.stem: Which four competencies make up the AI fluency framework?

options.a: Design, Draft, Deliver and Document, in that sequence
options.b: Define, Decide, Direct and Deploy, in that sequence
options.c: Detect, Diagnose, Debug and Deploy, in that sequence
options.d: Delegation, Description, Discernment and Diligence

items.explanation: The 4D framework names those four; module 5 teaches them as delegate, describe, discern and take responsibility.

items.stem: Which check matters most for a builder using Claude-generated code?

options.a: Counting how many lines the code contains
options.b: Running and testing it before it ships
options.c: Asking Claude whether it believes it is correct
options.d: Reading only the comments the code contains

items.explanation: Builders owe discernment of code and user experience: run it, test it, review it.

items.stem: What is the right use of Claude for learning in a course?

options.a: As a ghostwriter whose finished essay is handed in unchanged
options.b: As a way to get around the rules that the course sets
options.c: As a complete replacement for all of the course reading
options.d: As a partner that asks and explains while the student thinks

items.explanation: A student should not delegate the thinking the course exists to build.

items.stem: Which hidden risk does the page name for non-profits?

options.a: Writing the reports in plain language
options.b: Overstating results to a funder
options.c: Working alongside volunteers on projects
options.d: Keeping the records in a spreadsheet

items.explanation: Impact claims and statistics must be checked against the source before they reach a funder.

items.stem: For a maker, what should stay with the person?

options.a: Resizing and formatting the finished files
options.b: Transcribing the recorded interviews by hand
options.c: The idea, the voice and the final choices
options.d: Making variants for each different platform

items.explanation: Delegate production tasks, but keep the part that makes the work theirs.

items.stem: Which field is listed among the Usage Policy's high-risk uses?

options.a: Employment and housing decisions
options.b: Weather forecasts for a local newspaper
options.c: Recipe suggestions for a cooking site
options.d: Travel itineraries for a holiday company

items.explanation: Legal, health, insurance, finance, employment and housing, academic testing and media are high-risk uses.

items.stem: Which data class is normally allowed in any tool without a special check?

options.a: Public material
options.b: Internal material
options.c: Confidential material
options.d: Regulated material

items.explanation: Public data is free to use; internal needs an approved tool, and the other classes need stronger controls.

items.stem: A team asks whether replacing names with codes makes records anonymous. What is the right answer?

options.a: Yes, since any code at all makes records anonymous
options.b: No, because a separate key can reverse the substitution
options.c: Yes, as long as the codes are chosen at random
options.d: No, because codes are usually longer than names

items.explanation: Pseudonymised data is still personal data under many rules.

items.stem: A free-plan user wants her chats kept out of model improvement. Which option exists?

options.a: Clear the browser cache after finishing each session
options.b: Write a note in each chat asking it not to train
options.c: Use a much shorter prompt at the start of the chat
options.d: Use incognito sessions, which are excluded from training use

items.explanation: Incognito chats are excluded from improvement even when the setting is on; a request in a chat is not a control.

items.stem: Which habit limits prompt injection through email content?

options.a: Ask the assistant to ignore any hidden text it finds
options.b: Turn on every available connector for completeness
options.c: Keep a person confirming actions that send or delete
options.d: Use Skip all approvals to avoid interrupting the task

items.explanation: Keep a person on consequential steps and limit what Claude can do.

items.stem: Who should receive a report of a suspected leak first?

options.a: The whole team, at the next regular meeting
options.b: The security or IT contact, straight away
options.c: The vendor, through its public discussion forum
options.d: A colleague who works outside the company

items.explanation: A leak or a suspicious file is reported quickly, because waiting lets it spread.

items.stem: Which exam is aimed at professionals who use the assistant as a productivity tool?

options.a: Claude Certified Developer, Foundations
options.b: Claude Certified Architect, Foundations
options.c: Claude Certified Architect, Professional
options.d: Claude Certified Associate, Foundations

items.explanation: The Associate exam is for business users of Claude and needs no software-development experience.

items.stem: What decides pass or fail on the Claude exams?

options.a: The total scaled score, with 720 needed
options.b: The percentage reached in each separate domain
options.c: The number of attempts the candidate has made
options.d: The minutes that are left when the last item is done

items.explanation: Domain percentages guide revision but do not decide the result.

items.stem: A candidate's registered name differs from her photo ID. When must it be corrected?

options.a: At check-in, by explaining the difference to the proctor
options.b: After the exam, by lodging an appeal about the result
options.c: Before scheduling, through the support contact
options.d: It never matters, since the proctor sees the booking

items.explanation: The name must match exactly, and a correction is made before scheduling.

items.stem: Which behaviour counts as misconduct during an exam?

options.a: Using scratch paper that the provider supplies
options.b: Asking the proctor about a technical fault
options.c: Using an AI assistant for help
options.d: Taking a break that was approved in advance

items.explanation: The Exam Policy lists using AI products during the exam among prohibited activities.

items.stem: How long must a candidate wait to retake after the second failed attempt?

options.a: 30 days
options.b: 14 days
options.c: 90 days
options.d: 12 months

items.explanation: The waits are 14, 30 and 90 days after the first, second and third failed attempts.

items.stem: In a scenario question, what should you read first?

options.a: The longest option, since it is often the best
options.b: The last option, since it is placed there for a reason
options.c: The first sentence only, and then the options
options.d: The ask, then the situation with it in mind

items.explanation: The working method starts with reading the ask first.
